name: Neo-fascism
summary: Neo-fascism is the post-1945 continuation of fascism: ultranationalist, authoritarian and hostile to liberal democracy, Marxism and market capitalism, though often working through elections under a democratic veneer. It stresses national and increasingly European identity, strong leadership, hierarchy, opposition to immigration and a third-way economy of state direction and welfare for nationals.
scope: The mainstream of postwar neo-fascism as represented by the Italian Social Movement (MSI) and its heirs such as CasaPound, read alongside Eco's account of eternal fascism and the Wikipedia overview. It excludes interwar fascism proper (see fascism), neo-Nazi accelerationism and post-fascist parties that have renounced the label.

keyFigures.role: French writer who argued fascism should survive as a metapolitical project

sources.usedFor: The 14 features of eternal fascism: tradition, action, fear of difference, hierarchy, heroism, machismo, selective populism.

sources.title: CasaPound: 'Entreremo in Parlamento, e tutti dovranno fare i conti con noi' (interview with Simone Di Stefano)
sources.author: Linkiesta, February 2018
sources.usedFor: A neo-fascist leader's own program: citizenship by descent, exit from euro and EU, tariffs, birth allowance, migrant removal, Libya.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a stated aim; inferred from the postwar fascist-lineage tradition of an active state caring for the national community.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Adherents split between a social, anti-bourgeois wing and a conservative wing; no wage doctrine is stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Neo-fascists present themselves as a third way against market capitalism and neoliberalism.

public-ownership.rationale: CasaPound proposes a state holding for strategic industries on the old IRI model and nationalizing the central bank.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed as a doctrine; the movement attacks finance but also courts middle-class resentment of taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Fascist-lineage doctrine puts labor in state-recognized bodies and rejects class conflict, so independent unions are viewed warily.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is respected but subordinate to the nation; inferred from the movement's anti-liberal stance.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The third-way, anti-neoliberal stance favors subordinating business to national goals.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is favored for natives (see the birth income), though the stress is on the nation, not on welfare as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Corporatist class collaboration rather than worker ownership is the lineage's answer; the RSI's 'socialising' rhetoric is a minority echo.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Law-and-order authoritarianism makes security trade-offs acceptable; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from order, discipline and traditional-values emphasis.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Neo-fascist groups are the usual targets of such laws and present themselves as defenders of free expression within democracy.

strong-leader.rationale: Many parties are organized on the Fuhrerprinzip, and Eco's list includes a leader speaking for a monolithic People.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition centers on a strong sovereign state; Di Stefano calls for rebuilding strong states.

limit-guns.rationale: Cult of heroism sits against a state monopoly on force; no documented doctrine.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law and order and military virtues are standard themes of the MSI and its successors.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from moral traditionalism and machismo.

decide-locally.rationale: The MSI favored a centralised state and opposed regional devolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from contempt for weakness and the law-and-order outlook.

traditional-family.rationale: Neo-fascism is ultraconservative and natalist; CasaPound proposes a monthly payment per child.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Eco notes intolerance of nonstandard sexuality; some groups have accepted civil unions, so the answer is not uniform.

abortion-legal.rationale: Genuinely split between natalist traditionalists and groups that accept abortion rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Split between clerical, regime-style conservatives and secular or pagan currents.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial supremacy and white nationalism are listed among neo-fascist traits, and the movement rejects redress policies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Eco's machismo feature and ultraconservatism imply a belief in natural sex roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Intense nationalism and cultural preservation are almost always central.

gradual-change.rationale: Movements seek radical national rebirth and glorify action over reflection.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to immigration is a core issue; CasaPound would block illegal and limit legal immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Neo-fascists are nationalist and Eurosceptic; CasaPound wants out of the euro and the EU.

free-trade.rationale: Protectionism: Di Stefano speaks of tariffs up to 100 percent.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is the core of the ideology.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Force is favored for national interest (e.g. Libya), not for human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Nativism and anti-immigration stance make this the opposite of the position.

limit-growth.rationale: Autarkic, pro-production nationalism; eco-fascist strands exist but are marginal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No common line; some strands are environmental, others dismissive.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Eco notes rejection of modernism and the Enlightenment as a feature.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the pursuit of national self-sufficiency.

revolution-justified.rationale: Anti-system rhetoric and radical rebirth, though most parties now work through elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: Eco notes distrust of intellectuals and a primacy of action over thought.

central-planning.rationale: State direction of strategic sectors, not full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The lineage keeps private enterprise under national direction rather than ownership by workers.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the tradition; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Benefits are tied to nationals and to births, not unconditional; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism and autarky are explicit, e.g. tariffs of up to 100 percent.

state-directs-investment.rationale: CasaPound proposes an IRI-style public holding for strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Third-position anti-capitalism leans toward broad national ownership (housing mortgage schemes); inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: CasaPound would nationalize the Bank of Italy, not abolish central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is a legacy of the fascist lineage and the MSI included corporatist currents.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bardeche held single parties are not essential, and today's parties compete in multiparty systems.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The MSI's regime wing was monarchist, its movement wing republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Neo-fascism opposes liberal democracy even where it competes inside it.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscitary rhetoric exists, but the leader speaks for the People rather than citizens legislating.

right-to-secede.rationale: Unity of the nation; MSI opposed regionalism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Eco's features include hierarchy, elitism and contempt for the weak.

political-violence-never.rationale: Neo-fascist groups have used violence and the milieu celebrates heroism, though parties disavow it publicly.

war-builds-character.rationale: Eco: life is permanent struggle and heroism the norm.

separate-church-state.rationale: Split: laicist currents vs clerical conservatives.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred; nationalism rather than scripture grounds law.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Racial or ethnic nationalism is core, with citizenship by descent only.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejects Marxism and class conflict in favor of the nation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy and contempt for the weak.

civilizational-union.rationale: Postwar neo-fascists moved toward a shared pan-European identity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individuals are subordinated to the nation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Eco: individuals have no rights, only the People.

limit-population.rationale: Natalism: CasaPound proposes a payment per child for national families.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anti-modern traditionalism exists, but most parties are pro-industrial.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cult of tradition conflicts with disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Cult of tradition and a mythic golden age.

direct-action.rationale: Street activism and political violence are documented, though parties mostly use elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred; violence and hierarchy are used for ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nationalist state project incompatible with it.

production-for-use.rationale: Third-position critique of profit-driven markets; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejects the Marxist account of class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Neo-fascism opposes Marxism and class rule, so a working-class dictatorship is rejected outright.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist account rejected, though war is held to flow from national struggle.

taxation-theft.rationale: Strong state and duties to community.

harm-principle.rationale: Individuals have no rights against the People.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Citizens are bound to the nation.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a moral and national entity.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom as duty vs material aid; no clear line.

media-academia-power.rationale: Obsession with elite plots is an Eco feature; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial supremacy is listed among neo-fascism's features.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist currents and Third Position lean this way.

total-state.rationale: Fascist-lineage ideal, but Bardeche argued the apparatus was not essential and parties wear a democratic veneer.

national-rebirth.rationale: A golden age and a humiliated people fit Eco's features.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Split between irredentism and defensive pan-European policy.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths are not a stated aim.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Bardeche's metapolitical approach, but Eco notes anti-intellectualism.

universal-morality.rationale: Eco notes rejection of the Enlightenment.

single-common-good.rationale: A monolithic People and unitary nation.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Documented split: the MSI backed Israel, other wings were pro-Arab.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: CasaPound would erase the balanced-budget rule.

force-without-un.rationale: Di Stefano would act unilaterally in Libya and distrusts international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Eco notes irrationalism and action over reflection.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits are tied to nationals, e.g. births to Italian parents.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Duty to the community is central, so inferred support for conditioning benefits on work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rejects class conflict and corporatist cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The cult of tradition makes heritage institutions something to preserve, not sacrifice.

dominated-front.rationale: Split between anti-Atlantic and pro-Western wings.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: White-nationalist wings favor it; Italian lineages do not.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: National self-sufficiency and autarky imply favoring domestic energy production; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nation defined by descent, so assimilation is not accepted as sufficient.

elite-replacement.rationale: Plot obsession; replacement theory is cited by neo-fascist violence.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Machismo and traditional sex roles mean adherents deny that society is structured to disadvantage women.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from respect for the military and police and hostility to retrospective liability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The strong, sovereign, directing state is central, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Fear of difference and racial supremacy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Neo-fascists reject socialism, so the question about its internationalist conditions does not engage them.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalists defend their own states' founding and Mosley-style colonial Europe; inferred rejection of the label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary nation under one law is the inferred preference, though religion is not a core issue.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No documented doctrine; religion is secondary to the nation for most adherents.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No documented doctrine; the issue is not part of the European neo-fascist agenda.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Split between laicist currents and clerical conservatives, with no uniform stance.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The question is framed for socialist states; neo-fascists favor strong states but no stated view here.

population-transfer.rationale: Citizenship stripped and people sent back.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Force and struggle are valued as virtues, so a rule against initiating force is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Eco's account has life as permanent struggle, which this view echoes between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Neo-fascists were the usual targets; the MSI was kept out of the constitutional arch.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican idea is foreign to a movement stressing duty and hierarchy; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Leninist working-class vanguard is rejected, though elite leadership is valued in other forms.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Contempt for the weak; welfare for nationals.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Homeownership for nationals via social mortgage.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporatist doctrine replaces strikes with state-mediated bargaining; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pronatalist neo-fascists reject blaming population growth for poverty.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hierarchy and leadership would be undermined by choosing officials by chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian outlook favors strong emergency powers against internal enemies.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Selective populism: attacks on corrupt parliaments are central to Eco's account, and neo-fascists denounce political elites.

party-controls-media.rationale: Neo-fascists favor a strong authoritarian state that guides opinion, though some work through electoral politics and press freedom for themselves; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Fascism fused party and state, but neo-fascists in the MSI tradition favored a centralised presidential state commanding the forces; no clear party-over-state line, inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: CasaPound wants citizenship by descent and opposes ius soli, which implies a long and restrictive path for immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The neo-fascist tradition has no stated policy on official pay; adherents range from social anti-bourgeois to conservative views.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fascist-lineage parties like the MSI valued hierarchy and unity of command, and Eco lists obedience and a leader cult among traits of Ur-Fascism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: CasaPound calls for leaving the euro and the EU, though some neo-fascists back a Europe-wide nationalism, which makes a binding union contested.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The MSI program called for a centralised presidential state, and strong leadership is a defining neo-fascist feature.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Neo-fascists are split between Catholic traditionalists and pagan or secular currents; no common doctrine on church governance, inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Neo-fascism puts the nation and the state above clergy, though some currents work closely with traditionalist Catholics; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Ultranationalism requires loyalty to the nation in war and treats defeatism as betrayal.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Authoritarian, traditionalist currents favor policing culture for national morals, but no source states a censorship program; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Strong-leader doctrine implies leaders should serve as long as they hold support; inferred, not stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Neo-fascists favor authority from above over mid-term popular control of officials; inferred from their critique of liberal democracy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents split between Europeanist alliance with other nationalists and a sovereigntist exit from NATO; no firm line.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A third-way corporatist economy respects private property and ownership; abolishing rental housing is not a stated aim; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Fascism's cult of hierarchy and a disciplined state with a military leadership stands against an armed citizenry replacing the army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Fascist tradition romanticises the soil and peasantry against decadent cities; inferred from Eco's account of tradition.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Neo-fascists back ethnic-national unity and the Europeanist idea of a larger nation, so they favor reuniting divided nations.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Eco notes fascism's distrust of intellectuals and critical thought, and its populism against elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Neo-fascism holds a hierarchical view of peoples and fears difference, so it rejects cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Neo-fascists favor harsh punishment and the MSI and its heirs have supported the death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Adherents oppose gender-equality teaching as against traditional family roles; inferred from Eco's machismo and tradition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents are split between a Catholic wing and a pagan or secular wing and there is no stated line.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditionalist and machismo values suggest restriction, but this is not a stated aim; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: CasaPound wants ius sanguinis written into the constitution and ius soli opposed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on a single national culture suggests little support for minority-language rights; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minority religions cut against a unified national identity; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Eco says fascism fears difference and demands conformity and a cult of tradition, hostile to eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: CasaPound demands exit from the euro and defiance of creditors, so repudiating external debts fits, but cancelling poor countries' debts is not stated; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The third-position tradition stresses national sovereignty and an anti-capitalist economy, so independence without economic change is thought hollow; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The MSI favored a strong presidential republic, and no clear line on elected constituent assemblies is stated; adherents are split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Neo-fascists reject liberal democracy and place national strength above individual freedoms, and Eco's account notes hostility to critical pluralism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Neo-fascists put duty to the nation first, want migrants removed and would focus aid on nationals.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Strong nationalism and rejection of dependence on foreign powers imply support for a national deterrent; inferred, since strands differ on NATO.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The MSI backed a centralised presidential state, which fits a directly elected leader; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: CasaPound wants exit from the euro and monetary control back with the state, so independence from national government is opposed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Ultranationalists treat the national territory as sacred and do not trade it away.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Third Position economy subordinates property to the nation, with state direction in the national interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The classification of the USSR is not addressed; neo-fascists oppose Marxism but also reject market capitalism, so no clear stance; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between ecological strands and growth-minded ones.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents split between Atlanticist anti-communism in the MSI tradition and sovereigntist rejection of alliances in CasaPound.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: neo-fascism is irredentist and nationalist and does not value the consent of annexed peoples.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: the MSI courted Catholic opinion and neo-fascists prize tradition, so state control of churches is not an aim.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The MSI program sought a centralised presidential state above parties; inferred that the leader stands above faction.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Territorial integrity and national unity are core nationalist commitments, supporting force against secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Neo-fascism favors a centralised unitary state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is mostly secular-nationalist or Catholic, and divine-descent monarchism is a marginal Evolian strand.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the third-way economy of state direction and welfare for nationals, which does not favor a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Neo-fascism stresses race, blood and hierarchy, so character is seen as largely innate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from Eco's account of will and action over law, and the leader's primacy.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the futurist heritage and the Earth-bound nationalism pull in opposite directions.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: neo-fascism favors a unitary corporatist state with a single leadership, not a mix of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Eco lists heroism and the leader as features, and a strong leader embodying the nation is a stable theme.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; adherents likely split between traditionalist and father's-rights views.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Neo-fascism rejects Marxism and class-based socialism in favour of national unity; inferred from its hostility to Marxism.

land-redistribution.rationale: No program of breaking up estates; the Third Position economy protects national property, so inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed as a program; adherents focus on migrants and national return rather than a general right of return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Postwar fascists revived claims to lost territories on national grounds; inferred from the ultranationalism of the MSI tradition.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not an aim of the movement; inferred from its focus on the nation rather than on religious law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Neo-fascists back restrictions on Islamic dress rather than mandates on women; inferred from their anti-Muslim immigration stance.

common-currency.rationale: CasaPound’s leader calls for leaving the euro and the EU and returning to national monetary control.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Neo-fascism stresses a Europeanist unity of European peoples across borders; inferred as a kin-based union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Neo-fascists want a culturally and ethnically uniform nation, not self-governing minority institutions; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Neo-fascists treat minorities as outsiders and favour ethnic homelands; inferred from their immigration policy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Eco’s account stresses tradition, will and the cult of action over materialist explanation, and neo-fascists oppose Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: A state-directed Third Position economy sits uneasily with free-competition policy; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state direction of the economy under a strong state, which would rescue national firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Eco describes selective populism in which the Leader voices the people’s will, and the MSI wanted a centralised presidential state over liberal checks.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Eco’s machismo trait and the traditional gender roles of the movement imply opposition to quotas; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: CasaPound calls for tariffs and exit from the euro and EU, and Third Position economics favours national economic independence.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Neo-fascists reject international liberal trade regimes and supranational conditions; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Heroism, duty and sacrifice are core traits of eternal fascism, but no source addresses work incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Eco’s cult of action and the movement’s documented ties to political violence suggest sympathy for vanguard action; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Eco lists hierarchy and tradition as fascist traits, but republican MSI-lineage groups do not defend titles; inferred and leaning against.

history-own-civilization.rationale: National and European identity are central, so history is taught around them; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Neo-fascist traditions inherit imperial and hierarchical views; CasaPound's Libya policy shows interest in influence abroad, but tutelage is rarely stated.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ultranationalism makes national pride and symbols central to education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents prefer nationals by descent and oppose minority preferences; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: The third-way economy and anti-euro stance favor state control over money and finance; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: No stated position; adherents split between corporatist and conservative wings.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The MSI and heirs revived imperial and Mediterranean claims, but this is inferred, not a stated aim for every strand.

delink-world-market.rationale: Tariffs and autarky are urged for their own nation, with no stated view on poor countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses national solidarity across classes.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Neo-fascists reject liberal individual rights but favor discrimination for national and racial reasons; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Neo-fascism is hostile to liberal democracy, and Eco notes its rejection of rights-based pluralism.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Neo-fascists are anti-imperialist in rhetoric, but the issue is not documented as a position.

elective-rulers.rationale: The MSI favored a directly elected presidential state, and neo-fascists are mostly republican. Inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Eco's Ur-Fascism rejects disagreement as treason and holds that the national will is voiced by the leader.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Neo-fascism stresses obedience to authority and the state; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The MSI sought a centralised presidential state and attacked parliamentary democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Adherents are not documented as taking a side on animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: no tradition of animal-use abolition, with some humane concern.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchy with duties of leaders toward the national community is a fascist theme; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ur-Fascism prizes action for action's sake, heroism and the cult of participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Neo-fascists attack consumer mass society; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: They hold that liberal elites control culture and media; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Third Position economics opposes global capitalism and finance; CasaPound wants to leave the euro and EU. Inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: CasaPound wants citizenship and national preference based on descent, favoring natives.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: CasaPound's program calls for tariffs and exit from the euro and EU to restore national economic sovereignty.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism has been part of the MSI tradition; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Ethnic-national primacy of native peoples in their territory is implied by the nationalism of this tradition; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The MSI and heirs rejected antifascism as a foundation of the republic.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Neo-fascists are anti-communist but reject the idea that fascism is equivalent to communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not documented, since the issue is American; no position inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Cult of tradition and heroes (Eco) implies preserving monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Machismo and cult of manhood in Eco, though welfare for men is not stated; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Adherents are not documented as taking a side.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Neo-fascism rejects liberal universalism, stressing national and European identity and distinct civilizations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The MSI and heirs have close ties to the military; Eco notes the cult of heroism and order.

paid-care-work.rationale: CasaPound proposes a birth allowance to support mothers; recognition of care work is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Eco's traditionalism and the movement's organic national community, which values family hierarchy.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the movement prefers leader-appointed hierarchy to election and does not stress examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: CasaPound's program calls for tariffs and national economic protection against foreign capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, family-centred outlook Eco describes.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: neo-fascism favours a strong centralised leader over instructed, recallable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from a third-way economy of state direction and welfare for nationals, not private pension markets.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: the nation outranks the individual, but the movement does not call for communal land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the MSI wanted a centralised presidential state with weakened parliament.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its national-identity emphasis; no source addresses language policy directly.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from CasaPound's nationals-first program and citizenship by descent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from Eco's account of fear of difference and hierarchy, which rejects equal-outcome tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to market capitalism and cult of heroism over comfort.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its militant nationalism and Libya policy; no source states it directly.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Adherents are split between Europeanist bloc loyalty and national sovereignty; no source addresses it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the Third Position hostility to market capitalism and finance, though neo-fascists blame globalist elites more than business as such.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Neo-fascists stress national sovereignty, and CasaPound's program calls for exiting the EU and curbing outside influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: CasaPound's program includes a birth allowance for Italian families and opposes immigration as a fix for demographic decline.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the priority given to nationals and the rooted community; local restriction itself is not a stated aim.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the third-way economy of state direction and welfare for nationals; no stated employer-of-last-resort policy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from hostility to liberal democracy and the glorification of struggle; Eco lists pacifism as trafficking with the enemy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Eco's Ur-Fascism and the MSI program stress hierarchy and obedience to the state and leader.

non-intervention.rationale: Neo-fascists oppose US and NATO intervention yet CasaPound urges action in Libya; positions are mixed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Neo-fascists favor corporatist bodies joining workers and employers, which is neither craft nor industrial unionism as stated.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Strands vary; some neo-fascists adopt conspiracy claims about Jews or Muslims, while the MSI mainstream emphasizes national and European identity.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Neo-fascism upholds the traditional family as the basis of the nation, so ending legal marriage runs against it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian state, Eco's selective populism and distrust of open liberal institutions.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the economic nationalism and tariffs in the program, which favor national rather than strictly local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Neo-fascism relies on hierarchical, disciplined organization with a leader, as with the MSI and CasaPound.

national-law-over-international.rationale: CasaPound wants to leave the euro and EU, and the MSI program stresses the sovereign national state.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by ancestry and culture, and MSI-lineage groups are mostly secular or pagan-leaning while some strands are Catholic traditionalist; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Citizenship should pass only by descent, not by birth on the national territory.
missingStatements.rationale: CasaPound wants ius sanguinis written into the constitution and ius soli opposed.

notes: Strands diverge: MSI-lineage groups are Italian and sometimes pro-Israel and Atlanticist, others anti-Western; many electoral parties disavow fascism, and most answers are inferred from a thin set of primary texts.
